newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain presents 21.01 pct Telefonica share offer.
newsitem.headline: Spain presents 21.01 pct Telefonica share offer.

text.p: Spain launched an ambitious 1997 privatisation programme on Friday by announcing plans to sell its final 21.01 percent stake in telecommunications group Telefonica de Espana.
The state intends to sell up to 196.74 million shares -- offering 20.9 percent of Telefonica through its holding company SEPPa and another 0.11 percent through its main holding company.
It has still to set the final number and price of the shares, the 10-page description of the offer said.
Telefonica shares closed higher on Friday at 3,055, compared with 1,690 a year ago.
The Telefonica sale will be the minority Popular Party government's second privatisation, following last month's successful offer of 3.81 percent Gas Natural.
But it is just the start of a punishing 1997 schedule.

The government, anxious to meet stringent economic criteria and join in the launch of Europe's common currency in 1999, has said it will follow up the Telefonica offer with the sales of its remaining stakes of 25 percent in banking group Argentaria and 10 percent in energy group Repsol.
It also plans to sell a portion of its 66 percent holding in electricity group Endesa.
The government has estimated 1997 privatisation revenues at 450 billion pesetas and analysts say it has budgeted conservatively.
